title: Gauss–Wantzel: the number-theoretic core for general n
problemStatement: Prove, for arbitrary n and with no axioms, the arithmetic characterization underlying Gauss–Wantzel: φ(n) is a power of two iff the odd part of n is a squarefree product of Fermat primes. The parent angle-trisection-oq-02-oq-02 axiomatizes the geometric equivalence; the sibling angle-trisection-oq-02-oq-03-ext only enumerates the totient condition for n ≤ 50.
significance: Isolates the assumption-free number theory of Gauss–Wantzel and extends the constructibility classification from n ≤ 50 to all n, answering an open question of the sibling entry.
knownResults: Gauss–Wantzel theorem (constructible n-gons ⇔ φ(n) a power of two)
Mathlib Nat.pow_of_pow_add_prime: 2^m+1 prime ⟹ m a power of two
currentState: Solved. 16 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide. Builds against Mathlib 4.26.0.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: general-n arithmetic core of Gauss–Wantzel proved, 0 axioms. Necessity (squarefree odd part + Fermat-form primes + sharp 2^(2^j)+1 form) and sufficiency (product form 2^a·∏ distinct odd Fermat primes) both established for arbitrary n.
insights: φ(n) a power of two ⟹ for each odd prime p∣n, φ(p^e)=p^(e-1)(p-1) divides φ(n)=2^k; the odd factor p^(e-1) forces e=1 (squarefree odd part) and (p-1)∣2^k forces p=2^m+1.
Mathlib's Nat.pow_of_pow_add_prime upgrades p=2^m+1 prime to the genuine Fermat form p=2^(2^j)+1, giving sharp necessity.
Sufficiency is clean via Finset.induction: distinct primes are coprime (Nat.coprime_primes + Nat.Coprime.prod_right), so Nat.totient_mul splits the totient and IsPow2.mul recombines.
Specific polygon constructibility (15, 240) and non-constructibility (7) follow as corollaries of the general theorems instead of by native_decide enumeration.
Inside `namespace Nat`, the token `Prime` resolves to `Nat.Prime`, so coprime_primes/dvd_prime_pow take Nat.Prime arguments directly (no .prime).
